passages.note: House Third Reading roll call recording Martinez's Y vote on HB2853.
Bill status page lists Martinez as a co-sponsor of HB2853.

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: Enacted text adds universal eligibility criteria with no income cap.

passages.provision_quote: "Qualified school" means a nongovernmental primary or secondary school or a preschool for pupils with disabilities that is located in this state or, for qualified students who reside within the boundaries of an Indian reservation in this state, that is located in an adjacent state and that is within two miles of the border of the state in which the qualified student resides, and that does not discriminate on the basis of race, color or national origin.
passages.note: Enacted text defines qualified school as any nongovernmental school.

rows.reasoning: Martinez co-sponsored HB2853 (2022) and voted Y on its House Third Reading. The enacted text's new "qualified student" definition covers any resident eligible to enroll in public school from preschool through grade twelve with no income cap, and "qualified school" is defined as any nongovernmental school, matching the universal and any-school clauses of "Providing universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family."
